properties.entry:
Notifications from ui-components show short messages as toasts, stacked in a corner of the window or in the middle of its top or bottom edge. Each has a header, with the icon of its type, a title and a button closing it, and a body, text or HTML. It stays until the user closes it, or goes after a timeout, which a bar along its bottom counts down, 5 seconds by default, while errors stay until closed; the countdown waits while the pointer is over the notification or the focus in it, and Escape closes the one that has the focus. There are four types, success, error, warning and information, and the page may have its own: the note below is violet and has a light bulb, from a class of the page's style sheet. Notifications are in the colors of the theme, and work under a strict Content Security Policy.

Choose a notification in the first form and show it via Ajax with show(Notification). In Wicket the feedback messages of the page become notifications too: save the second form without a name, and the required field's error shows as one; with a name, the page's success() does. Every page of this demo shows its feedback messages this way, with the Notifications of its base page. The React and Svelte tabs show the same with their Notifications.

"Show after a redirect" keeps the notification in the session with SessionNotifications.show(Notification) and goes to a new page, whose Notifications show it, as after signing in elsewhere and coming back. The feedback messages of the session, such as getSession().success(), come over a redirect the same way. This is Wicket only: React and Svelte show their notifications in the page they are in.
